submitted.rationale: Best measured EQE was 0.101% at Sb 0.45 (index 22). EQE rose steadily as Sb went down from 0.63 (0.081%) to 0.52 (0.089%) to 0.45 (0.101%). This composition lies in the YSbO4-rich region. MACE puts YSbO4 on the convex hull, and MEGNet gives it the lowest band gap of the stable ternaries (2.97 eV, HSE). The Y-rich side should form wide-gap Y3SbO7 (3.6 eV) and Y2O3. All merit budget is used.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.081% EQE, lower than index 22. The Sb-rich side (Y3Sb5O12, gap 3.4 eV) does not help.
These should form Y3SbO7 and Y2O3, which have wide gaps (3.6 eV and above) and should absorb little at 2.1 eV. They were not measured because the budget ran out.

consultations.verdict: Support: Y-rich Y3SbO7 has wide HSE gap (3.6 eV) and is inert at 2.1 eV; Sb-rich phases (Y3Sb5O12 on hull, gap 3.4; YSbO4 gap 3.0) have lower gaps and Sb lone-pair states, so the Sb-rich end (index 28, Sb 0.63) is most likely to absorb at 2.1 eV.

Support: MACE puts YSbO4 on the hull (Ehull 0), and its MEGNet HSE gap (2.97 eV) is the lowest of the stable ternaries, so the Sb~0.5 composition (index 24) should form this phase and absorb closest to 2.1 eV.

Weak support / largely uninformative: the MEGNet gap for the metastable YSbO3 perovskite (0.29 eV) is likely a small-cell artifact and isn't a hull phase, so it doesn't favour any composition. Measured EQE rose from Sb 0.63 (0.081) to Sb 0.52 (0.089), and Y3SbO7 on the Y-rich side is wide-gap (3.6 eV). Index 22 (Sb 0.45), in the YSbO4-rich two-phase region, is the best remaining guess for a peak.
